meta.purpose: Regression fixtures for the FORMATTER of the real agent that replaces the scripted flows. A real model will write its own prose; it must still produce this shape — the same plan granularity, the same tool sequence, citation chips in the same places relative to the claims they support, and the same closing standing note.
capturedFromProse: plan step text — a plan step is not prose, it is the plan
bold lead-in labels — the answer’s section structure
the closing standing note — the honesty policy, kept verbatim because a paraphrase is not a regression target
clarify questions and option labels — the fork is the shape
deliberatelyNotCaptured: toolCall durationMs — playback timing, not answer shape

planStepRole.parse: Restate the question in ontology terms — field ids, organism ids, target.
planStepRole.guard: A check that must pass before the answer may be written — counter-evidence, isPrimary, conflict detection, a refused unit conversion, a negative result to flag.
planStepRole.shape: Organise the retrieved evidence: split, separate, rank, map.
planStepRole.deliver: Assemble, report or state the answer.
planStepRole.unclassified: No rule fired. Add a rule rather than leaving this in a fixture.

chipSlot.sentence-lead: First token of a sentence. The dominant paper-chip position: the entry is the grammatical subject of the claim it supports.
chipSlot.sentence-final: Last token before the sentence terminator.
chipSlot.clause-final: Last token before a comma or semicolon.
chipSlot.mid-sentence: Inside a sentence with words on both sides.
chipSlot.cell-only: The table cell contains nothing but the chip.
chipSlot.cell-lead: First token of a table cell, with more after it.
chipSlot.cell-trailing: Last token of a table cell — the cell states a value, the chip cites it.
chipSlot.cell-mid: Inside a table cell with content on both sides.

chipPrecededBy.block-start: Chip is the first token of its block — paper chip in subject position.
chipPrecededBy.cell-start: Chip is the first token of a table cell.
chipPrecededBy.bold-quantity: Immediately after a bolded number — "**500 mg/L** [[r-H2-1]]".
chipPrecededBy.quantity: Immediately after an unbolded number within the last three tokens.
chipPrecededBy.bold-word: Immediately after a bolded non-numeric span.
chipPrecededBy.word: Mid-prose, after ordinary words — the chip discharges a clause, not a number.
chipPrecededBy.chip: Immediately after another chip — a chip run.
chipPrecededBy.punctuation: After a comma, dash or colon.

chipFollowedBy.period: Sentence ends immediately after the chip.
chipFollowedBy.comma: Clause ends immediately after the chip.
chipFollowedBy.semicolon: Clause ends immediately after the chip.
chipFollowedBy.em-dash: An aside opens immediately after the chip.
chipFollowedBy.chip: Another chip follows — a chip run.
chipFollowedBy.word: The sentence continues past the chip.
chipFollowedBy.block-end: Chip is the last token of its block.
chipFollowedBy.cell-end: Chip is the last token of its table cell.

footerClaim.curator-transcription: States the numbers came from a curator note, not a source PDF.
footerClaim.catalogued-not-ingested: Names the entries as catalogued — metadata plus a note, no full text.
footerClaim.verify-before-citing: Tells the reader to verify before citing.
footerClaim.not-read-from-source: Names something the corpus has not read and therefore cannot claim.
footerClaim.authored-judgement: Marks part of the answer as the agent’s own judgement rather than corpus fact.
footerClaim.scope-limit: Bounds what the cited evidence covers — measured on a reporter, on the wild type, on a different organism.
footerClaim.absence-is-a-finding: States that the absence itself is the curated result.

meta.determinism: Derived from a fixed array in declaration order; maps are keyed in codepoint order, never locale order. Two consecutive runs are byte-identical.

renderingContract.note: Read out of the files named below at capture time. Nothing here is computed from FLOWS, so it goes stale if those files change and must be re-read rather than trusted.

answerRendering.recordChipRule: an id starting "r-" renders as a record chip (deep-links to the span); anything else renders as a paper chip
answerRendering.unresolvedChipRendering: red error chip reading "Source unavailable", never silent
answerRendering.stripChartAppearsWhen: four or more cited records share one ontology field and convert to its canonical unit

retrievalRendering.layout: two-column card grid beneath the tool row
retrievalRendering.emptyRetrievalArray: renders the "No passages in this corpus match" callout
retrievalRendering.absentRetrievalKey: renders nothing beneath the tool row

toolRowRendering.collapsed: wrench icon, tool name, args joined as "k=v · k=v", durationMs
toolRowRendering.methodLine: args.method, when present, is printed unfolded beneath the row — scripted flows do not set it, live retrieval does

promptEntryPoints.note: The six chips on the empty Ask screen. Each is one flow trigger verbatim, so a click is an exact match rather than a fuzzy one — this is the demo’s entry path and the first thing to break if triggers are edited. Matched here by a documented normalizer (lowercase; non-alphanumerics to space; collapse whitespace), which is deliberately looser than the matcher in src/sim/chat.ts. This fixture pins the entry RELATION, not the matcher.
